title: Chatbot product profile (product.yaml)
description: The product this chatbot answers about, in business terms: the things people ask about, how a click opens them, who the user is, and the product's words. ProductProfile checks the file against this schema when it loads.

version.description: The layout of this file. Always 2.

entities.description: The things people ask about, one block each, keyed by the name a person uses for one of them ("ticket", "order").

table.description: The view that holds one row per thing. Leave out when it has none of its own.

words.description: Every word a person types to name it, singular and plural. A question naming one of these starts a new topic instead of continuing the last one.

id.description: The column holding its id. A filter on it pins the conversation to one record, named "<entity> <id>".

same_id_as.description: Other names the same id goes by in an answer, such as an old column name.

title.description: The readable column a person clicks instead of the id.

reference.description: The column holding its business reference number.

kind.description: The column naming its type. Never offered as a grouping. One entity at most.

colour.description: The column holding its colour code (see `colours`). Every row that carries its id gets a colour strip. One entity at most; needs `table` and `id`.

default_rule.description: The business rule applied when nobody asks otherwise, such as open-only. Must be a single table.column = 'value' rule.

open.description: What a click does. Exactly one of url, download or popup.

url.description: A page opened in a new tab. {id} is replaced by the value of `id`.

encode.description: How {id} is written into the url: plain (default) or base64.

download.description: The column holding a stored file's address; the click downloads it.

popup.description: The name of a popup the app already has, such as BODetails.

param.description: The name the popup expects the id under.

button.description: Show the click as a button with this text in its own column, instead of making a cell clickable.

id_column_endings.description: Any column whose name ends like this holds an id, even when no entity names it.

columns.description: Facts about one column, keyed by its name.

unit.description: A unit the name does not say; the heading becomes "<name> (<unit>)".

group.description: false: never suggest grouping by it, such as free text that differs on every row.

words.description: A word inside any column name, and how to write it (sla: SLA).

phrases.description: Part of a column name replaced before it is split into words.

suggestions.description: The follow-up chips offered after an answer.

sort_by.description: Parts of column names worth sorting by, most interesting first.

never_correct.description: Ordinary words one letter from a database word, which must never be changed into it.

colours.description: Colours with a meaning, keyed by name. A chart label naming one is drawn in it.

code.description: How the data stores it, and the CSS class the app paints the colour strip with.

users.description: Who the signed-in user is. The Drupal user id is the product's user id.

table.description: The view with one row per user.

departments.description: Where a user's departments are. Leave out when the product has none.

table.description: The view with one row per user and department.

messages.description: Product words in the messages a user sees when a query fails.

icon.description: One of the app's starter icons.

prompt.description: The product's words inside the fixed system prompt. Each value is pasted into a sentence exactly as written; read the sentence with the value in it.

database.description: "You generate read-only SQL for a PostgreSQL <database> analytics database."

rule_terms.description: "...the business rules -- they define what terms like <rule_terms> mean in SQL."

two_level_example.description: "...when a question asks for counts at two levels at once -- <two_level_example>. Joining the child table repeats every parent row..."

colour_note.description: A sentence of its own after "Leave it out when no colour means anything." Empty or absent: none.

chart_scope.description: "It must cover exactly the same records as the main query: keep every filter, <chart_scope> and rule the main query applies..."

explanation_example.description: Whole sentences after "...do not describe how the query works.": a good explanation, then the SQL-like one to avoid.

clarify_example.description: Whole sentences after "Never name a table or a column in it, never quote SQL.": a good clarifying question, then the one to avoid.
